def fit(  # noqa: C901
    self,
    X_train: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    X_test: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    y_train: Union[pd.Series, np.ndarray],
    y_test: Union[pd.Series, np.ndarray],
) -> Union[pd.DataFrame, Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]]:
    """Fit estimators and score on test data.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X_train : array-like
        Training feature matrix.
    X_test : array-like
        Testing feature matrix.
    y_train : array-like
        Training target vector.
    y_test : array-like
        Testing target vector.

    Returns
    -------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        Metrics for every model.
    predictions : pandas.DataFrame
        Only returned when ``self.predictions`` is True.
        Prediction rows preserve the index of ``X_test``.
    """
    # Results of a previous fit() must not leak into this one.
    self.models = {}
    self.errors = {}
    self.tuned_scores_ = None
    self.tuned_params_ = {}
    self.tuned_models_ = {}

    # Auto-convert PySpark/Dask DataFrames
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = _auto_convert_inputs(
        X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test
    )
    # One-column targets such as df[["price"]] are used as vectors.
    if np.ndim(y_train) == 2 and np.shape(y_train)[1] == 1:
        y_train = np.ravel(y_train)
    if np.ndim(y_test) == 2 and np.shape(y_test)[1] == 1:
        y_test = np.ravel(y_test)

    # Dataset size warnings
    if hasattr(X_train, "shape"):
        n_samples, n_features = X_train.shape
        if n_samples > 100_000:
            logger.warning(
                "Large dataset detected (%d samples). Training all models may "
                "take a long time. Consider using a subset or setting max_models/timeout.",
                n_samples,
            )
        if n_features > 500:
            logger.warning(
                "High-dimensional dataset (%d features). Some models may be slow "
                "or fail. Consider dimensionality reduction.",
                n_features,
            )

    _validate_fit_inputs(X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test)
    self._validate_target(y_train)
    X_train, X_test = prepare_dataframes(X_train, X_test)
    self._feature_columns = list(X_train.columns)
    preprocessor = build_preprocessor(X_train, self.categorical_encoder)

    estimator_list = self._get_estimator_list()
    step_name = self._estimator_step_name()

    # When GPU requested, append cuML GPU-accelerated models if available
    if self.use_gpu:
        cuml_models = get_cuml_models()
        if cuml_models:
            existing_names = {n for n, _ in estimator_list}
            for cuml_name, cuml_cls in cuml_models.items():
                if cuml_name not in existing_names:
                    # Only add if compatible with current task type
                    try:
                        from sklearn.base import ClassifierMixin, RegressorMixin
                        if step_name == "classifier" and issubclass(cuml_cls, ClassifierMixin):
                            estimator_list.append((cuml_name, cuml_cls))
                        elif step_name == "regressor" and issubclass(cuml_cls, RegressorMixin):
                            estimator_list.append((cuml_name, cuml_cls))
                        elif step_name not in ("classifier", "regressor"):
                            estimator_list.append((cuml_name, cuml_cls))
                    except TypeError:
                        # cuML classes may not work with issubclass
                        estimator_list.append((cuml_name, cuml_cls))
            logger.info(
                "cuML (RAPIDS) is available — added %d GPU-accelerated models.",
                len([n for n in cuml_models if n not in existing_names]),
            )

    # Apply max_models limit
    if self.max_models is not None:
        estimator_list = estimator_list[: self.max_models]

    results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    predictions_dict: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    progress_bar = notebook_tqdm if _use_notebook_tqdm else tqdm
    total = len(estimator_list)
    tracker = RunTracker(_mlflow if self.mlflow_enabled and MLFLOW_AVAILABLE else None)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        if self.ignore_warnings:
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        for idx, (name, model) in enumerate(
            progress_bar(estimator_list, disable=(self.verbose == 0))
        ):
            start = time.perf_counter()
            run_started = tracker.start(f"{self.__class__.__name__}-{name}", model_name=name)
            metrics: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
            try:
                model_kwargs = self._model_kwargs(model)
                pipe = Pipeline(
                    steps=[
                        ("preprocessor", clone(preprocessor)),
                        (step_name, model(**model_kwargs)),
                    ]
                )

                with time_limit(self.timeout):
                    pipe.fit(X_train, y_train)
                fit_time = time.perf_counter() - start
                if self.timeout and fit_time > self.timeout:
                    # The limit could not be enforced preemptively
                    # (Windows, worker thread, or a long C call).
                    raise TimeoutException(
                        f"Training took {fit_time:.2f}s, exceeding timeout={self.timeout}s"
                    )

                cv_metrics = self._run_cv(pipe, X_train, y_train, name) if self.cv else {}
                metrics = self._compute_metrics(pipe, X_test, y_test, X_train)
                metrics["name"] = name
                metrics["time"] = time.perf_counter() - start
                metrics.update(cv_metrics)
                if self.custom_metric is not None:
                    metrics["custom_metric"] = self._custom_metric_value(
                        y_test, pipe.predict(X_test), name
                    )
                if self.predictions:
                    predictions_dict[name] = pipe.predict(X_test)
            except Exception as exc:
                metrics = None
                self.errors[name] = exc
                if isinstance(exc, TimeoutException):
                    logger.info("%s skipped: %s", name, exc)
                elif not self.ignore_warnings:
                    logger.warning("%s model failed to execute: %s", name, exc)
            else:
                # Only models that produced scores are kept.
                self.models[name] = pipe
                results.append(metrics)
                if self.verbose > 0:
                    self._log_verbose(name, metrics)
                if run_started:
                    tracker.call(self._log_mlflow_metrics, metrics, pipe, X_train, name)
            finally:
                if run_started:
                    tracker.end()

            if self.progress_callback is not None:
                self.progress_callback(name, idx + 1, total, metrics)

    scores = self._build_scores_dataframe(results)

    # Store for tuning access
    self._last_X_train = X_train
    self._last_y_train = y_train
    self._last_preprocessor = preprocessor
    self._last_estimator_list = estimator_list

    # Phase 2: Auto-tune top-k if requested
    if self.tune and len(scores) > 0:
        self.tuned_scores_ = self._run_tuning(scores, X_train, y_train, preprocessor, estimator_list)

    if self.predictions:
        prediction_index = X_test.index if isinstance(X_test, pd.DataFrame) else None
        predictions_df = pd.DataFrame(
            predictions_dict, index=prediction_index if predictions_dict else None
        )
        return scores, predictions_df
    return scores, pd.DataFrame()

def explain(
    self,
    X_test: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    y_test: Union[pd.Series, np.ndarray],
    method: str = "permutation",
    n_repeats: int = 10,
    max_samples: int = 100,
    tuned: bool = False,
) -> Union[pd.DataFrame, Dict[str, np.ndarray]]:
    """Explain model predictions with feature importance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X_test : array-like
        Test feature matrix.
    y_test : array-like
        Test target.
    method : str, optional (default='permutation')
        Explanation method: 'permutation' (zero deps) or 'shap'.
    n_repeats : int, optional (default=10)
        Repeats for permutation importance.
    max_samples : int, optional (default=100)
        Max samples for SHAP explanations.
    tuned : bool, optional (default=False)
        Explain the tuned models (``tuned_models_``) instead.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame or dict
        For 'permutation': DataFrame with features as rows, models as columns.
        For 'shap': dict mapping model name to SHAP values array.
    """
    models = self._models_for(tuned, "No models fitted. Call fit() first.")
    X_test, y_test = _auto_convert_inputs(X_test, y_test)
    X_test = self._to_frame(X_test)

    if method == "permutation":
        from lazypredict.explainability import explain_permutation

        return explain_permutation(
            models, X_test, y_test,
            n_repeats=n_repeats,
            random_state=self.random_state,
            n_jobs=self.n_jobs,
        )
    elif method == "shap":
        from lazypredict.explainability import explain_shap

        return explain_shap(
            models, X_test,
            step_name=self._estimator_step_name(),
            max_samples=max_samples,
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown method: {method}. Use 'permutation' or 'shap'.")

def predict(

    X_test: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    model_name: Optional[str] = None,
    tuned: bool = False,
) -> Union[Dict[str, np.ndarray], np.ndarray]:
    """Make predictions using fitted models.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X_test : array-like
        Test feature matrix (NumPy input gets the training column names).
    model_name : str or None, optional (default=None)
        Specific model to use. If None, returns predictions from all models.
    tuned : bool, optional (default=False)

        instead of the benchmarked ones.

    -------
    dict or numpy.ndarray

    """
    models = self._models_for(tuned, "No models have been fitted yet. Please call fit() first.")
    X_test = self._to_frame(X_test)

        if model_name not in models:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Model '{model_name}' not found. "
                f"Available models: {list(models.keys())}"
            )
        return np.asarray(models[model_name].predict(X_test))

    return {name: model.predict(X_test) for name, model in models.items()}

def save_models(self, path: str) -> None:
    """Save all fitted models to disk using joblib.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : str
        Directory path to save models.
    """
    import os
    import joblib

    if len(self.models) == 0:
        raise ValueError("No models have been fitted yet. Please call fit() first.")

    os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
    for name, model in self.models.items():
        filepath = os.path.join(path, f"{name}.joblib")
        joblib.dump(model, filepath)
        logger.info("Saved %s to %s", name, filepath)

def load_models(self, path: str) -> Dict[str, Pipeline]:
    """Load models from disk.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : str
        Directory path containing saved models.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Mapping of model name to loaded Pipeline.
    """
    import os
    import joblib

    if not os.path.isdir(path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Directory not found: {path}")

    for filename in os.listdir(path):
        if filename.endswith(".joblib"):
            name = filename[:-7]  # strip .joblib
            filepath = os.path.join(path, filename)
            self.models[name] = joblib.load(filepath)
            logger.info("Loaded %s from %s", name, filepath)

    return self.models

@click.command()
@click.version_option(version=__version__, prog_name="lazypredict")
@click.option(
    "--task",
    type=click.Choice(["classification", "regression"]),
    help="Type of ML task.",
)
@click.option(
    "--input",
    "input_file",
    type=click.Path(exists=True, dir_okay=False),
    help="Path to CSV dataset.",
)
@click.option("--target", type=str, help="Name of the target column.")
@click.option("--test-size", type=float, default=0.2, help="Fraction of data for testing.")
@click.option("--random-state", type=int, default=42, help="Random seed.")
def main(task, input_file, target, test_size, random_state):
    """LazyPredict — quickly benchmark scikit-learn models on a dataset."""
    if input_file is None and target is None and task is None:
        click.echo("LazyPredict CLI — run `lazypredict --help` for usage.")
        click.echo("Example: lazypredict --task classification --input data.csv --target label")
        return

    missing = [
        option
        for option, value in (("--task", task), ("--input", input_file), ("--target", target))
        if value is None
    ]
    if missing:
        raise click.UsageError(f"Missing option(s): {', '.join(missing)}.")
    if not 0 < test_size < 1:
        raise click.BadParameter("must be between 0 and 1 (exclusive).", param_hint="--test-size")

    import pandas as pd
    from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

    df = pd.read_csv(input_file)
    if target not in df.columns:
        raise click.BadParameter(
            f"column {target!r} not found in {input_file}.", param_hint="--target"
        )

    X = df.drop(columns=[target])
    y = df[target]
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=test_size, random_state=random_state
    )

    if task == "classification":
        from lazypredict.Supervised import LazyClassifier
        model = LazyClassifier(verbose=0, ignore_warnings=True, random_state=random_state)
    else:
        from lazypredict.Supervised import LazyRegressor
        model = LazyRegressor(verbose=0, ignore_warnings=True, random_state=random_state)

    scores, _ = model.fit(X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test)
    if scores.empty:
        name, error = next(iter(model.errors.items()), ("", "no model was selected"))
        raise click.ClickException(
            f"No model could be trained ({len(model.errors)} failed); {name}: {error}"
        )
    click.echo(scores.to_string())

def get_gpu_model_params(model_class, use_gpu: bool) -> dict:
    """Return GPU-related keyword arguments for a model class.

    Inspects the model class module to determine if it supports GPU
    acceleration and returns the appropriate kwargs.

    Supported GPU backends:

    - **XGBoost**: ``device="cuda"``
    - **LightGBM**: ``device="gpu"``
    - **CatBoost**: ``task_type="GPU"``
    - **cuML (RAPIDS)**: No extra params needed (GPU-native).

    Parameters
    ----------
    model_class : type
        The model class to inspect.
    use_gpu : bool
        Whether GPU usage has been requested by the user.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Keyword arguments to pass to the model constructor for GPU support.
        Empty dict if the model does not support GPU or ``use_gpu`` is False.
    """
    if not use_gpu:
        return {}

    module = getattr(model_class, "__module__", "") or ""

    # XGBoost: use device="cuda"
    if "xgboost" in module:
        if is_gpu_available():
            return {"device": "cuda"}
        else:
            logger.warning(
                "GPU requested for %s but CUDA is not available. "
                "Falling back to CPU.",
                model_class.__name__,
            )
            return {}

    # LightGBM: use device="gpu"
    if "lightgbm" in module:
        if is_gpu_available():
            return {"device": "gpu"}
        else:
            logger.warning(
                "GPU requested for %s but CUDA is not available. "
                "Falling back to CPU.",
                model_class.__name__,
            )
            return {}

    # CatBoost: use task_type="GPU"
    if "catboost" in module:
        if is_gpu_available():
            return {"task_type": "GPU"}
        else:
            logger.warning(
                "GPU requested for %s but CUDA is not available. "
                "Falling back to CPU.",
                model_class.__name__,
            )
            return {}

    # cuML (RAPIDS): models are GPU-native, no extra params needed
    if "cuml" in module:
        if is_gpu_available():
            return {}
        else:
            logger.warning(
                "GPU requested for %s (cuML) but CUDA is not available. "
                "cuML requires a CUDA-capable GPU.",
                model_class.__name__,
            )
            return {}

    return {}

def get_cuml_models() -> dict:
    """Return a mapping of sklearn model names to cuML GPU equivalents.

    cuML (RAPIDS) provides GPU-accelerated drop-in replacements for many
    scikit-learn estimators.  This function returns the available ones.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``{sklearn_name: cuml_class}`` for available cuML models.
        Empty dict if cuML is not installed.
    """
    models: dict = {}
    try:
        import cuml  # noqa: F401
    except ImportError:
        return models

    # Classifiers
    _cuml_classifiers = [
        ("cuML_LogisticRegression", "cuml.linear_model", "LogisticRegression"),
        ("cuML_RandomForestClassifier", "cuml.ensemble", "RandomForestClassifier"),
        ("cuML_KNeighborsClassifier", "cuml.neighbors", "KNeighborsClassifier"),
        ("cuML_SVC", "cuml.svm", "SVC"),
    ]
    # Regressors
    _cuml_regressors = [
        ("cuML_LinearRegression", "cuml.linear_model", "LinearRegression"),
        ("cuML_Ridge", "cuml.linear_model", "Ridge"),
        ("cuML_Lasso", "cuml.linear_model", "Lasso"),
        ("cuML_ElasticNet", "cuml.linear_model", "ElasticNet"),
        ("cuML_RandomForestRegressor", "cuml.ensemble", "RandomForestRegressor"),
        ("cuML_KNeighborsRegressor", "cuml.neighbors", "KNeighborsRegressor"),
        ("cuML_SVR", "cuml.svm", "SVR"),
    ]

    for name, mod_path, cls_name in _cuml_classifiers + _cuml_regressors:
        try:
            import importlib
            mod = importlib.import_module(mod_path)
            models[name] = getattr(mod, cls_name)
        except (ImportError, AttributeError):
            pass

    return models

def adjusted_rsquared(r2: float, n: int, p: int) -> float:
    """Calculate adjusted R-squared.

    Parameters
    ----------
    r2 : float
        R-squared value.
    n : int
        Number of observations.
    p : int
        Number of predictors.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Adjusted R-squared value, or NaN when it is undefined
        (``n - p - 1 <= 0``, i.e. no more observations than predictors).
    """
    dof = n - p - 1
    if dof <= 0:
        return float("nan")
    return 1 - (1 - r2) * ((n - 1) / dof)

def mean_absolute_percentage_error(
    y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray
) -> float:
    """Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).

    Undefined when y_true contains zeros; those entries are excluded.

    Parameters
    ----------
    y_true : array-like
        Actual values.
    y_pred : array-like
        Predicted values.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        MAPE as a percentage (0–100+).
    """
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)
    y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float)
    mask = y_true != 0
    if not mask.any():
        return np.inf
    return float(
        np.mean(np.abs((y_true[mask] - y_pred[mask]) / y_true[mask])) * 100
    )

    y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray
) -> float:
    """Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE).

    More balanced than MAPE; handles zeros better.

    Parameters
    ----------
    y_true : array-like
        Actual values.
    y_pred : array-like
        Predicted values.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        SMAPE as a percentage (0–200).
    """
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)
    y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float)
    denominator = np.abs(y_true) + np.abs(y_pred)
    mask = denominator != 0
    if not mask.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(
        np.mean(
            2.0 * np.abs(y_true[mask] - y_pred[mask]) / denominator[mask]
        )
        * 100
    )

def mean_absolute_scaled_error(
    y_true: np.ndarray,
    y_pred: np.ndarray,
    y_train: np.ndarray,
    seasonal_period: int = 1,
) -> float:
    """Mean Absolute Scaled Error (MASE).

    Scale-free metric relative to the in-sample naive forecast error.
    ``seasonal_period=1`` compares against a random-walk naive forecast;
    values > 1 use seasonal naive.

    Parameters
    ----------
    y_true : array-like
        Actual test values.
    y_pred : array-like
        Predicted values.
    y_train : array-like
        Training series used to compute the naive scaling factor.
    seasonal_period : int
        Seasonal period for the naive baseline (1 = non-seasonal). When the
        training series is not longer than one season, the non-seasonal
        naive forecast is used instead.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        MASE value.  Values < 1 beat the naive baseline; NaN when
        ``y_train`` has fewer than two values.
    """
    if int(seasonal_period) < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"seasonal_period must be >= 1, got {seasonal_period!r}")
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)
    y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float)
    y_train = np.asarray(y_train, dtype=float)
    if len(y_train) <= seasonal_period:
        seasonal_period = 1
    if len(y_train) < 2:
        return float("nan")
    naive_errors = np.abs(y_train[seasonal_period:] - y_train[:-seasonal_period])
    scale = np.mean(naive_errors)
    if scale == 0:
        return np.inf
    return float(np.mean(np.abs(y_true - y_pred)) / scale)

    y_true: np.ndarray,

def categories_as_strings(X) -> np.ndarray:
    """Normalise categorical input before imputation and encoding.

    ``category``, nullable ``string``, pandas 3 ``str`` and mixed-type
    ``object`` columns become one ``object`` array of ``str`` values with
    ``np.nan`` for every kind of missing value (``None``, ``pd.NA``, ``NaN``),
    so they are imputed and encoded the same way even when the training and
    test data use different dtypes.
    """
    frame = X if isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame) else pd.DataFrame(X)
    columns = [
        _column_as_strings(frame.iloc[:, i]).to_numpy(dtype=object)
        for i in range(frame.shape[1])
    ]
    if not columns:
        return np.empty((len(frame), 0), dtype=object)
    return np.column_stack(columns)

def get_categorical_encoder(
    encoder_type: str = "onehot", cardinality: str = "low"
) -> Pipeline:
    """Get categorical encoder pipeline based on encoder type and cardinality.

    Parameters
    ----------
    encoder_type : str, optional (default='onehot')
        Type of encoder: 'onehot', 'ordinal', 'target', or 'binary'.
    cardinality : str, optional (default='low')
        Cardinality level: 'low' or 'high'.

    Returns
    -------
    Pipeline
        Sklearn pipeline with imputer and encoder.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If *encoder_type* is not one of the recognised values.
    """
    imputer = SimpleImputer(strategy="constant", fill_value="missing")

    if encoder_type == "onehot":
        if cardinality == "low":
            encoder = OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", sparse_output=False)
        else:
            encoder = OrdinalEncoder(
                handle_unknown="use_encoded_value", unknown_value=-1
            )
    elif encoder_type == "ordinal":
        encoder = OrdinalEncoder(
            handle_unknown="use_encoded_value", unknown_value=-1
        )
    elif encoder_type == "target":
        if not CATEGORY_ENCODERS_AVAILABLE:
            logger.warning(
                "category_encoders not installed. Falling back to ordinal encoding. "
                "Install with: pip install category_encoders"
            )
            encoder = OrdinalEncoder(
                handle_unknown="use_encoded_value", unknown_value=-1
            )
        else:
            encoder = TargetEncoder(handle_unknown="value", handle_missing="value")
    elif encoder_type == "binary":
        if not CATEGORY_ENCODERS_AVAILABLE:
            logger.warning(
                "category_encoders not installed. Falling back to onehot encoding. "
                "Install with: pip install category_encoders"
            )
            encoder = OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", sparse_output=False)
        else:
            encoder = BinaryEncoder(handle_unknown="value", handle_missing="value")
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown encoder type: {encoder_type}. "
            f"Choose from {VALID_ENCODERS!r}"
        )

    return Pipeline(
        steps=[
            (
                "as_strings",
                FunctionTransformer(categories_as_strings, feature_names_out="one-to-one"),
            ),
            ("imputer", imputer),
            ("encoding", encoder),
        ]
    )

def get_card_split(
    df: pd.DataFrame, cols: Union[pd.Index, list], n: int = 11
) -> Tuple[pd.Index, pd.Index]:
    """Split categorical columns into two lists based on cardinality.

    Parameters
    ----------
    df : pandas.DataFrame
        DataFrame from which the cardinality of the columns is calculated.
    cols : array-like
        Categorical columns to evaluate.
    n : int, optional (default=11)
        Columns with more than *n* unique values are considered high cardinality.

    Returns
    -------
    card_low : pandas.Index
        Columns with cardinality <= *n*.
    card_high : pandas.Index
        Columns with cardinality > *n*.
    """
    cols = pd.Index(cols)
    cond = df[cols].nunique() > n
    card_high = cols[cond]
    card_low = cols[~cond]
    return card_low, card_high

def prepare_dataframes(
    X_train: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    X_test: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return ``X_train`` and ``X_test`` as DataFrames with the same column names.

    Array-likes (NumPy arrays, lists) take the training DataFrame's column
    names, or ``feature_0 .. feature_n`` when the training data has none; in
    that case a DataFrame ``X_test`` is relabelled by position. ``X_test``
    keeps its index whenever it is a DataFrame. Numeric columns of ``object``
    arrays (e.g. ``df.to_numpy()`` with a text column) get numeric dtypes, and
    non-string column labels become strings.
    """
    if isinstance(X_train, pd.DataFrame):
        X_train = with_string_column_names(X_train)
        if isinstance(X_test, pd.DataFrame):
            X_test = with_string_column_names(X_test)
        else:
            X_test = _array_to_frame(X_test, X_train.columns)
        return X_train, X_test

    X_train = _array_to_frame(X_train)
    columns = pd.Index([f"feature_{i}" for i in range(X_train.shape[1])])
    X_train.columns = columns
    if isinstance(X_test, pd.DataFrame):
        X_test = X_test.set_axis(columns, axis=1)
    else:
        X_test = _array_to_frame(X_test, columns)
    return X_train, X_test

def with_string_column_names(X: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return *X* with ``str`` column labels.

    scikit-learn's ``ColumnTransformer`` treats integer labels as positions,
    so the columns ``[1, 2, 3]`` of a headerless CSV would select the wrong
    columns or fail.
    """
    if all(isinstance(column, str) for column in X.columns):
        return X
    return X.rename(columns=str)

def times_as_numbers(X) -> np.ndarray:
    """Encode datetime columns as days since 1970 and timedeltas as seconds.

    Missing values (``NaT``) become ``np.nan`` for the imputer that follows.
    """
    frame = X if isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame) else pd.DataFrame(X)
    columns = []
    for i in range(frame.shape[1]):
        column = frame.iloc[:, i]
        if pd.api.types.is_timedelta64_dtype(column.dtype):
            values = pd.to_timedelta(column).dt.total_seconds()
        else:
            moments = pd.to_datetime(column, utc=True)
            values = (moments - pd.Timestamp(0, tz="UTC")) / pd.Timedelta(days=1)
        columns.append(np.asarray(values, dtype=float))
    return np.column_stack(columns) if columns else np.empty((len(frame), 0))

def build_preprocessor(
    X_train: pd.DataFrame, categorical_encoder: str
) -> ColumnTransformer:
    """Build a ColumnTransformer for the given data.

    Numeric and boolean columns are imputed and scaled, categorical columns
    are imputed and encoded, and datetime/timedelta columns are converted to
    numbers (days since 1970, seconds) and then treated as numeric.
    """
    temporal_features = pd.Index(
        [col for col, dtype in X_train.dtypes.items() if _is_temporal_dtype(dtype)]
    )
    # timedelta64 counts as np.number in pandas; it goes to the temporal branch.
    numeric_features = X_train.select_dtypes(include=[np.number, "bool"]).columns.difference(
        temporal_features, sort=False
    )
    categorical_features = pd.Index(
        [col for col, dtype in X_train.dtypes.items() if _is_categorical_dtype(dtype)]
    )

    categorical_low, categorical_high = get_card_split(X_train, categorical_features)

    cat_low = get_categorical_encoder(categorical_encoder, cardinality="low")
    cat_high = get_categorical_encoder(categorical_encoder, cardinality="high")

    return ColumnTransformer(
        transformers=[
            ("numeric", numeric_transformer, numeric_features),
            (
                "temporal",
                Pipeline(
                    steps=[
                        ("as_numbers", FunctionTransformer(times_as_numbers, feature_names_out="one-to-one")),
                        ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="mean")),
                        ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
                    ]
                ),
                temporal_features,
            ),
            ("categorical_low", cat_low, categorical_low),
            ("categorical_high", cat_high, categorical_high),
        ]
    )

Auto-detect the dominant seasonal period.

Candidates are local peaks of the autocorrelation function (ACF) of the linearly detrended series that exceed 2.5 times Bartlett's standard error of its short-term autocorrelation (the lags before the ACF first reaches zero), so the seasonal pattern itself does not raise the bar. Each candidate is moved to the nearby lag where the values grouped by phase differ most, then confirmed by a one-way ANOVA of the values grouped by phase (Bonferroni-corrected over all ACF peaks) whose seasonal pattern must explain at least 20% of the variance. Of the confirmed periods, the shortest that is at least 85% as strong as the strongest is returned, so the fundamental period wins over its multiples. When the levels show no seasonality, the first differences are searched as well, which finds seasonality on top of a random walk.

Detection needs at least three full cycles; for shorter series pass seasonal_period to LazyForecaster instead.

def detect_seasonal_period(
    y: np.ndarray, max_period: int = 365
) -> Optional[int]:
    """Auto-detect the dominant seasonal period.

    Candidates are local peaks of the autocorrelation function (ACF) of the
    linearly detrended series that exceed 2.5 times Bartlett's standard error
    of its short-term autocorrelation (the lags before the ACF first reaches
    zero), so the seasonal pattern itself does not raise the bar. Each
    candidate is moved to the nearby lag where the values grouped by phase
    differ most, then confirmed by a one-way ANOVA of the values grouped by
    phase (Bonferroni-corrected over all ACF peaks) whose seasonal pattern
    must explain at least 20% of the variance. Of the confirmed periods, the
    shortest that is at least 85% as strong as the strongest is returned, so
    the fundamental period wins over its multiples. When the levels show no
    seasonality, the first differences are searched as well, which finds
    seasonality on top of a random walk.

    Detection needs at least three full cycles; for shorter series pass
    ``seasonal_period`` to ``LazyForecaster`` instead.

    Parameters
    ----------
    y : np.ndarray
        Time series values.
    max_period : int
        Maximum candidate period to consider.

    Returns
    -------
    int or None
        Detected seasonal period, or ``None`` if no significant
        seasonality is found.
    """
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    n = len(y)
    if n < 8 or not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
        return None
    # Degeneracy threshold from the centred series, so a large constant
    # offset does not hide the seasonal signal.
    centred = y - y.mean()
    scale = float(np.dot(centred, centred))
    if scale == 0:
        return None
    t = np.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, n)
    detrended = y - np.polyval(np.polyfit(t, y, 1), t)
    for series in (detrended, np.diff(y)):
        series = series - series.mean()
        if np.dot(series, series) <= 1e-12 * scale:
            continue
        period = _seasonal_period_of(series, max_period)
        if period is not None:
            return period
    return None

def create_lag_features(
    y: np.ndarray,
    n_lags: int = 10,
    n_rolling: Optional[Tuple[int, ...]] = None,
    X_exog: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Create lag features, rolling statistics, and a diff feature.

    Parameters
    ----------
    y : np.ndarray
        Time series values.
    n_lags : int
        Number of lag features (y_{t-1} … y_{t-n_lags}).
    n_rolling : tuple of int or None
        Window sizes for rolling mean and rolling std.
    X_exog : np.ndarray or None
        Exogenous features to append (shape ``(len(y), k)``).

    Returns
    -------
    X_features : np.ndarray
        Feature matrix of shape ``(n_valid, n_features)``.
    y_target : np.ndarray
        Target values aligned with the feature rows.
    """
    n_rolling = tuple(dict.fromkeys(n_rolling or (3, 7)))  # equal windows count once
    df = pd.DataFrame({"y": y})

    # Lag features
    for lag in range(1, n_lags + 1):
        df[f"lag_{lag}"] = df["y"].shift(lag)

    # Rolling statistics (shifted by 1 to avoid data leakage)
    for window in n_rolling:
        df[f"rolling_mean_{window}"] = df["y"].shift(1).rolling(window).mean()
        df[f"rolling_std_{window}"] = df["y"].shift(1).rolling(window).std()

    # First-difference feature
    df["diff_1"] = df["y"].diff().shift(1)

    # Drop rows with NaN
    df = df.dropna()
    y_target = df["y"].values
    X_features = df.drop(columns=["y"]).values

    # Append the exogenous variables of the rows that were kept
    if X_exog is not None:
        X_exog = np.asarray(X_exog)
        if X_exog.ndim == 1:
            X_exog = X_exog.reshape(-1, 1)
        if len(X_exog) != len(y):
            raise ValueError(
                f"X_exog has {len(X_exog)} rows but the series has {len(y)} values"
            )
        X_features = np.hstack([X_features, X_exog[df.index.to_numpy()]])

    return X_features, y_target

def next_step_features(
    history,
    n_lags: int,
    n_rolling: Optional[Tuple[int, ...]] = None,
    exog_row: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Feature row for the step right after *history*.

    Mirrors :func:`create_lag_features`: the row built from ``y[:t]`` here is
    identical to the training row of time ``t``.
    """
    n_rolling = tuple(dict.fromkeys(n_rolling or (3, 7)))
    features: List[float] = [history[-lag] for lag in range(1, n_lags + 1)]
    for window in n_rolling:
        recent = history[-window:]
        features.append(float(np.mean(recent)))
        # ddof=1 matches pandas' rolling().std() used for the training features.
        features.append(float(np.std(recent, ddof=1)) if len(recent) > 1 else 0.0)
    features.append(history[-1] - history[-2] if len(history) >= 2 else 0.0)
    if exog_row is not None:
        features.extend(np.asarray(exog_row, dtype=float).ravel().tolist())
    return np.array(features, dtype=float).reshape(1, -1)

) -> np.ndarray:
    """Multi-step recursive (autoregressive) forecast.

    At each step the model predicts the next value, which is then appended
    to the history before computing features for the following step.

    Parameters
    ----------
    estimator
        Fitted sklearn-compatible regressor.
    scaler : StandardScaler
        Fitted scaler used during training.
    y_history : np.ndarray
        Historical series used for context.
    horizon : int
        Number of future steps to predict.
    n_lags : int
        Number of lag features.
    n_rolling : tuple of int or None
        Rolling window sizes.
    X_exog : np.ndarray or None
        Exogenous features for the forecast period (shape ``(horizon, k)``).

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Array of length ``horizon`` with predicted values.
    """
    predictions: List[float] = []
    history = list(y_history)

    if X_exog is not None:
        X_exog = np.asarray(X_exog)
        if X_exog.ndim == 1:
            X_exog = X_exog.reshape(-1, 1)
        if len(X_exog) < horizon:
            raise ValueError(
                f"X_exog has {len(X_exog)} rows but {horizon} forecast steps were requested"
            )

    for step in range(horizon):
        exog_row = X_exog[step] if X_exog is not None else None
        X_step = scaler.transform(next_step_features(history, n_lags, n_rolling, exog_row))
        pred = float(estimator.predict(X_step)[0])
        predictions.append(pred)
        history.append(pred)

    return np.array(predictions)

    X_test: pd.DataFrame,
    y_test: Any,
    n_repeats: int = 10,
    random_state: int = 42,
    n_jobs: int = -1,

    n_jobs : int

    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame with features as rows, models as columns,
        values are mean importance scores.

    if not models:
        raise ValueError("No fitted models. Call fit() first.")

    if isinstance(X_test, np.ndarray):
        cols = [f"feature_{i}" for i in range(X_test.shape[1])]
        X_test = pd.DataFrame(X_test, columns=cols)

    feature_names = list(X_test.columns)
    importance_dict: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    for name, pipe in models.items():
        try:
            result = permutation_importance(
                pipe,
                X_test,
                y_test,
                n_repeats=n_repeats,
                random_state=random_state,
                n_jobs=n_jobs,
            )
            importance_dict[name] = result.importances_mean
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning("Permutation importance failed for %s: %s", name, exc)
            importance_dict[name] = np.full(len(feature_names), np.nan)

    df = pd.DataFrame(importance_dict, index=feature_names)
    df.index.name = "Feature"
    return df

def tune_supervised_optuna(
    model_name: str,
    model_class: Any,
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: Any,
    preprocessor: Any,
    scoring: str,
    cv: int = 5,
    n_trials: int = 50,
    timeout: Optional[float] = None,
    random_state: int = 42,
    n_jobs: int = -1,
    use_gpu: bool = False,
) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], float]:
    """Tune a single supervised model using Optuna.

    Trials that raise or produce NaN scores are recorded as failed and the
    search continues. The sampler is seeded with *random_state*.

    Returns
    -------
    best_params : dict
        Best hyperparameters found (including fixed values from the search
        space); empty when no trial completed.
    best_score : float
        Best mean cross-validation score (higher is better); NaN when no
        trial completed.
    """
    _check_optuna()
    from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

    space_fn = get_search_space(model_name)
    if space_fn is None:
        logger.info("No search space for %s, skipping tuning.", model_name)
        return {}, float("nan")
    fixed = _model_kwargs(model_class, random_state, use_gpu)

    def objective(trial):
        params = space_fn(trial)
        trial.set_user_attr("params", params)
        pipe = Pipeline([("preprocessor", clone(preprocessor)), ("model", model_class(**{**fixed, **params}))])
        return _cv_score(pipe, X_train, y_train, cv, scoring, n_jobs)

    study = optuna.create_study(
        direction="maximize", sampler=optuna.samplers.TPESampler(seed=random_state)
    )
    study.optimize(objective, n_trials=n_trials, timeout=timeout, catch=(Exception,))

    completed = [t for t in study.trials if t.state == optuna.trial.TrialState.COMPLETE]
    if not completed:
        return {}, float("nan")
    best = study.best_trial
    return dict(best.user_attrs.get("params", best.params)), float(study.best_value)

def tune_supervised_sklearn(
    model_name: str,
    model_class: Any,
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: Any,
    preprocessor: Any,
    scoring: str,
    cv: int = 5,
    n_iter: int = 50,
    random_state: int = 42,
    n_jobs: int = -1,
    use_gpu: bool = False,
    timeout: Optional[float] = None,
) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], float]:
    """Tune a single supervised model by random search.

    Candidates are sampled (``ParameterSampler``) from distributions derived
    from the model's Optuna search space and scored by cross-validation, like
    ``RandomizedSearchCV``. Candidates that fail (e.g. ``n_neighbors`` larger
    than a fold) score NaN instead of aborting the search. With *timeout*, no
    new candidate is started once that many seconds have passed.
    """
    from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

    param_dist = _optuna_to_sklearn_dist(model_name)
    if not param_dist:
        return {}, float("nan")

    fixed = _model_kwargs(model_class, random_state, use_gpu)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout if timeout is not None else None
    best: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    best_score = float("nan")
    for params in ParameterSampler(param_dist, n_iter=n_iter, random_state=random_state):
        if deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            break
        pipe = Pipeline([
            ("preprocessor", clone(preprocessor)),
            ("model", model_class(**{**fixed, **params})),
        ])
        try:
            score = _cv_score(pipe, X_train, y_train, cv, scoring, n_jobs)
        except Exception as exc:  # invalid parameter combination
            logger.debug("%s candidate %s failed: %s", model_name, params, exc)
            continue
        if np.isfinite(score) and not score <= best_score:
            best, best_score = dict(params), score
    return best, best_score

def tune_supervised_flaml(
    model_name: str,
    model_class: Any,
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: Any,
    preprocessor: Any,
    scoring: str,
    cv: int = 5,
    n_trials: int = 50,
    timeout: Optional[float] = None,
    random_state: int = 42,
    n_jobs: int = -1,
    use_gpu: bool = False,
) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], float]:
    """Tune a single supervised model with FLAML's cost-frugal search.

    FLAML searches its own space for the matching learner; the parameters of
    the best estimator it finds are then scored through the lazypredict
    pipeline, so ``best_score`` is comparable with the other backends.
    Models FLAML has no learner for return ``({}, nan)``.
    """
    _check_flaml()
    from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

    learner = _FLAML_LEARNERS.get(model_name)
    if learner is None:
        logger.info("FLAML has no learner for %s, skipping tuning.", model_name)
        return {}, float("nan")

    automl = AutoML()
    settings = {
        "task": "classification" if _is_classifier_class(model_class) else "regression",
        "metric": _flaml_loss(scoring),
        "estimator_list": [learner],
        "max_iter": n_trials,
        "time_budget": timeout if timeout is not None else 60,
        "eval_method": "cv",
        "n_splits": cv,
        "n_jobs": n_jobs,
        "seed": random_state,
        "verbose": 0,
    }
    X_prepared = preprocessor.fit_transform(X_train, y_train)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        automl.fit(X_prepared, np.asarray(y_train), **settings)

    estimator = getattr(automl.model, "estimator", None)
    if estimator is None or type(estimator).__name__ != model_class.__name__:
        return {}, float("nan")
    # Keep what FLAML changed: values that differ from the defaults, and
    # parameters a default instance does not report at all (LightGBM's
    # max_bin, every CatBoost parameter).
    defaults = model_class().get_params()
    best = {
        key: value
        for key, value in estimator.get_params().items()
        if key not in _NON_MODEL_PARAMS and (key not in defaults or defaults[key] != value)
    }
    fixed = _model_kwargs(model_class, random_state, use_gpu)
    pipe = Pipeline([("preprocessor", clone(preprocessor)), ("model", model_class(**{**fixed, **best}))])
    return best, _cv_score(pipe, X_train, y_train, cv, scoring, n_jobs)

def tune_top_k(
    scores_df: pd.DataFrame,
    models: Dict[str, Any],
    estimator_list: List[Tuple[str, Any]],
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: Any,
    preprocessor: Any,
    scoring: str,
    top_k: int = 5,
    n_trials: int = 50,
    timeout: Optional[float] = None,
    random_state: int = 42,
    n_jobs: int = -1,
    backend: str = "optuna",
    use_gpu: bool = False,
    cv: int = 5,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tune the top-k models from the initial ranking.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores_df : pd.DataFrame
        Scores DataFrame from initial fit (index = model names).
    models : dict
        Fitted model pipelines.
    estimator_list : list
        List of (name, class) tuples from _get_estimator_list.
    X_train, y_train : array-like
        Training data.
    preprocessor : ColumnTransformer
        Preprocessor template (cloned for every candidate).
    scoring : str
        Scoring metric string (e.g. 'balanced_accuracy', 'r2').
    top_k : int
        Number of top models to tune.
    n_trials : int
        Trials (Optuna/FLAML) or sampled candidates (sklearn) per model.
    timeout : float or None
        Seconds per model tuning (Optuna and FLAML).
    random_state : int
        Random seed.
    n_jobs : int
        Parallel jobs.
    backend : str
        'optuna', 'sklearn', or 'flaml'.
    use_gpu : bool
        Whether GPU is enabled.
    cv : int
        Number of cross-validation folds.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        One row per model (index ``Model``) with ``Best Score`` (mean
        cross-validated score on the training data, higher is better),
        ``Best Params`` (a dict) and ``Status`` (``"tuned"``,
        ``"no search space"`` or ``"failed: ..."``). A model that cannot be
        tuned never aborts the others.
    """
    tuners = {
        "optuna": lambda name, cls: tune_supervised_optuna(
            name, cls, X_train, y_train, preprocessor, scoring, cv=cv, n_trials=n_trials,
            timeout=timeout, random_state=random_state, n_jobs=n_jobs, use_gpu=use_gpu,
        ),
        "sklearn": lambda name, cls: tune_supervised_sklearn(
            name, cls, X_train, y_train, preprocessor, scoring, cv=cv, n_iter=n_trials,
            random_state=random_state, n_jobs=n_jobs, use_gpu=use_gpu, timeout=timeout,
        ),
        "flaml": lambda name, cls: tune_supervised_flaml(
            name, cls, X_train, y_train, preprocessor, scoring, cv=cv, n_trials=n_trials,
            timeout=timeout, random_state=random_state, n_jobs=n_jobs, use_gpu=use_gpu,
        ),
    }
    if backend not in tuners:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown backend: {backend}. Use 'optuna', 'sklearn', or 'flaml'.")
    supported = _FLAML_LEARNERS if backend == "flaml" else SEARCH_SPACES

    name_to_class = dict(estimator_list)
    results = []
    for model_name in list(scores_df.index[:top_k]):
        model_class = name_to_class.get(model_name)
        if model_class is None:
            continue
        row = {"Model": model_name, "Best Score": float("nan"), "Best Params": {}}
        if model_name not in supported:
            logger.info("No %s search space for %s, skipping.", backend, model_name)
            results.append({**row, "Status": "no search space"})
            continue

        logger.info("Tuning %s with %s backend...", model_name, backend)
        try:
            best_params, best_score = tuners[backend](model_name, model_class)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning("Tuning %s failed: %s", model_name, exc)
            results.append({**row, "Status": f"failed: {exc}"})
            continue
        if np.isnan(best_score):
            results.append({**row, "Status": "failed: no successful trial"})
            continue
        results.append({**row, "Best Score": best_score, "Best Params": best_params, "Status": "tuned"})

    columns = ["Model", "Best Score", "Best Params", "Status"]
    return pd.DataFrame(results, columns=columns).set_index("Model")

def tune_forecaster_optuna(
    model_name: str,
    wrapper,
    y_train: np.ndarray,

    seasonal_period: Optional[int],
    tune_metric: str = "RMSE",

    timeout: Optional[float] = None,
    random_state: int = 42,
    tune_seasonal: bool = False,
    horizon: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], float]:
    """Tune a single forecasting model using Optuna.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model_name : str
        Name of the forecaster.
    wrapper : ForecasterWrapper
        The forecaster wrapper instance (will be deep-copied per trial).
    y_train : np.ndarray
        Training time series.
    X_train : np.ndarray or None
        Exogenous features.
    seasonal_period : int or None
        Detected seasonal period.
    tune_metric : str
        Metric to optimize ('RMSE', 'MAE', 'MAPE', 'SMAPE', 'MASE').
    cv : int

    n_trials : int
        Number of Optuna trials.
    timeout : float or None
        Seconds limit per model tuning.
    random_state : int
        Random seed.
    tune_seasonal : bool
        If True, also search over seasonal_period values.
    horizon : int or None
        Forecast horizon; each CV fold forecasts this many steps.

    Returns
    -------
    best_params : dict

        ``order``); empty when no trial produced a finite score.
    best_score : float

    """

        raise ImportError(
            "optuna is required for tuning. Install with: pip install lazypredict[tune]"
        )

    from lazypredict.TimeSeriesForecasting import AutoARIMAForecaster

    space_fn = get_ts_search_space(model_name)
    if space_fn is None:
        logger.info("No search space for %s, skipping tuning.", model_name)
        return {}, float("inf")

    def objective(trial):
        params = space_fn(trial)
        if tune_seasonal and model_name in ("SARIMAX", "HoltWinters_Add", "HoltWinters_Mul"):
            candidates = _seasonal_candidates(
                len(y_train), seasonal_period,
                # A SARIMAX state space grows with the period; longer ones
                # need minutes and gigabytes per fit.
                max_period=AutoARIMAForecaster.MAX_SEASONAL_PERIOD if model_name == "SARIMAX" else None,
            )
            if candidates:
                params["seasonal_period"] = trial.suggest_categorical("seasonal_period", candidates)
        trial.set_user_attr("params", params)
        # MASE is scaled by the benchmark's seasonal period, not the trial's:
        # otherwise a period with a large naive error looks best.
        return _temporal_cv_error(
            wrapper, model_name, params, y_train, X_train,
            seasonal_period, tune_metric.lower(), cv, horizon=horizon,
        )

    study = optuna.create_study(
        direction="minimize", sampler=optuna.samplers.TPESampler(seed=random_state)
    )
    study.optimize(objective, n_trials=n_trials, timeout=timeout, catch=(Exception,))

    finished = [
        (float(t.value), t)
        for t in study.trials
        if t.state == optuna.trial.TrialState.COMPLETE
        and t.value is not None
        and np.isfinite(t.value)
    ]
    if not finished:
        return {}, float("inf")
    best_value, best = min(finished, key=lambda item: item[0])
    return dict(best.user_attrs.get("params", best.params)), best_value

def tune_top_k_forecasters(
    scores_df,
    models: Dict[str, Any],
    all_wrappers: List[Tuple[str, Any]],
    y_train: np.ndarray,
    X_train: Optional[np.ndarray],
    seasonal_period: Optional[int],
    top_k: int = 5,
    tune_metric: str = "RMSE",
    cv: int = 3,
    n_trials: int = 30,
    timeout: Optional[float] = None,
    random_state: int = 42,
    tune_seasonal: bool = False,
    refit: bool = True,
    horizon: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Tuple["pd.DataFrame", Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Tune the top-k forecasters from initial ranking.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores_df : pd.DataFrame
        Ranked model scores from initial benchmarking.
    models : dict
        Fitted model wrappers.
    all_wrappers : list of (name, wrapper) tuples
        All available forecaster wrappers.
    y_train : np.ndarray
        Training time series.
    X_train : np.ndarray or None
        Exogenous features.
    seasonal_period : int or None
        Seasonal period.
    top_k : int
        Number of top models to tune.
    tune_metric : str
        Metric to optimize.
    cv : int
        Number of CV folds.
    n_trials : int
        Optuna trials per model.
    timeout : float or None
        Seconds limit per model tuning.
    random_state : int
        Random seed.
    tune_seasonal : bool
        Search over seasonal_period values.
    refit : bool
        When True, refit each tuned model on full ``y_train`` with
        best parameters and return the fitted wrappers.

    Returns
    -------
    tune_results : pd.DataFrame
        One row per model (index ``Model``) with ``Best <tune_metric>`` (mean
        temporal-CV error of the best trial, lower is better), ``Best Params``
        (a dict) and ``Status`` (``"tuned"``, ``"no search space"`` or
        ``"failed: ..."``).
    tuned_models : dict
        ``{model_name: fitted_wrapper}`` when ``refit=True``,
        empty dict otherwise.
    """
    import pandas as pd

    top_model_names = list(scores_df.index[:top_k])
    name_to_wrapper = {name: w for name, w in all_wrappers}
    score_column = f"Best {tune_metric}"

    results = []
    tuned_models: Dict[str, Any] = {}

    for model_name in top_model_names:
        wrapper = name_to_wrapper.get(model_name)
        if wrapper is None:
            continue
        row = {"Model": model_name, score_column: float("nan"), "Best Params": {}}

        if get_ts_search_space(model_name) is None:
            logger.info("No search space for %s, skipping.", model_name)
            results.append({**row, "Status": "no search space"})
            continue

        logger.info("Tuning forecaster %s...", model_name)
        try:
            best_params, best_score = tune_forecaster_optuna(
                model_name, wrapper, y_train, X_train, seasonal_period,
                tune_metric=tune_metric, cv=cv, n_trials=n_trials,
                timeout=timeout, random_state=random_state,
                tune_seasonal=tune_seasonal, horizon=horizon,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning("Tuning %s failed: %s", model_name, exc)
            results.append({**row, "Status": f"failed: {exc}"})
            continue
        if not best_params:
            results.append({**row, "Status": "failed: no successful trial"})
            continue
        results.append({
            **row, score_column: best_score, "Best Params": best_params, "Status": "tuned",
        })

        # Refit with best params on full training data
        if refit:
            try:
                w = copy.deepcopy(wrapper)
                _apply_params_to_wrapper(w, model_name, best_params)
                w.fit(y_train, X_train)
                tuned_models[model_name] = w
                logger.info("Refit %s with best params.", model_name)
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.warning(
                    "Failed to refit %s with best params: %s", model_name, exc
                )

    columns = ["Model", score_column, "Best Params", "Status"]
    return pd.DataFrame(results, columns=columns).set_index("Model"), tuned_models

def ensemble_weighted_average(
    predictions: Dict[str, np.ndarray],
    scores: Dict[str, float],
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Inverse-error weighted average of predictions.

    Models with lower error get higher weight.

    Parameters
    ----------
    predictions : dict
        Mapping of model name to prediction array.
    scores : dict
        Mapping of model name to error metric (lower is better).

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Weighted-average predictions.
    """
    if not predictions:
        raise ValueError("No predictions to ensemble.")

    names = list(predictions.keys())
    arrays = np.array([predictions[n] for n in names])
    error_vals = np.array([scores.get(n, 1.0) for n in names])

    # Inverse error weights (add epsilon to avoid division by zero)
    eps = 1e-10
    inv_errors = 1.0 / (error_vals + eps)
    weights = inv_errors / inv_errors.sum()

    return np.average(arrays, axis=0, weights=weights)

def ensemble_stacking(
    predictions: Dict[str, np.ndarray],
    y_true: np.ndarray,
    pred_test: Optional[Dict[str, np.ndarray]] = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Stack predictions using a Ridge meta-learner.

    Fits a Ridge regression that maps the models' *validation* predictions
    to the true validation values, then applies it to their test
    predictions.

    Parameters
    ----------
    predictions : dict
        Mapping of model name to out-of-sample predictions for a validation
        period (not the period being evaluated).
    y_true : np.ndarray
        True values for that validation period.
    pred_test : dict
        Mapping of model name to the predictions to combine. Required:
        returning the meta-model's fit on the data it was trained on would
        overstate its accuracy.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Stacked predictions for ``pred_test``.
    """
    from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge
    from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
    from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

    if not predictions:
        raise ValueError("No predictions to ensemble.")
    if pred_test is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "pred_test is required: fit the meta-model on validation predictions "
            "and apply it to separate test predictions."
        )

    names = sorted(predictions.keys())
    X_stack = np.column_stack([predictions[n] for n in names])

    # Standardised inputs make the ridge penalty independent of the series'
    # units; on raw values it shrank small-valued series to their mean.
    meta = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), Ridge(alpha=1.0))
    meta.fit(X_stack, y_true)

    X_test_stack = np.column_stack([pred_test[n] for n in names])
    return np.asarray(meta.predict(X_test_stack))

def direct_forecast(
    estimator_class,
    y_train: np.ndarray,
    horizon: int,
    n_lags: int = 10,
    n_rolling: Tuple[int, ...] = (3, 7),
    X_exog: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    random_state: int = 42,
    use_gpu: bool = False,
    model_params: Optional[dict] = None,
    X_future: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Direct multi-step forecasting: train one model per horizon step.

    Model ``h`` (``h = 1..horizon``) learns to predict ``y[t + h - 1]`` from
    the lag features available at time ``t`` and, with exogenous variables,
    their values at the target time ``t + h - 1``; all models then predict
    from the lags after ``y_train`` and the matching row of ``X_future``.
    More accurate for long horizons but trains ``horizon`` separate models.

    Parameters
    ----------
    estimator_class : type
        Sklearn-compatible regressor class.
    y_train : np.ndarray
        Training time series.
    horizon : int
        Number of future steps.
    n_lags : int
        Number of lag features.
    n_rolling : tuple of int
        Rolling window sizes.
    X_exog : np.ndarray or None
        Exogenous features for the training period.
    random_state : int
        Random seed.
    use_gpu : bool
        Whether to use GPU.
    model_params : dict or None
        Extra model constructor params.
    X_future : np.ndarray or None
        Exogenous features for the forecast period, one row per step
        (required with ``X_exog``).

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Array of length ``horizon`` with direct forecasts.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``y_train`` is too short to train a model for every step.
    """
    X_lags, y_feat = create_lag_features(y_train, n_lags, n_rolling)
    n_rows = len(y_feat)
    if n_rows < horizon + 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Not enough history for direct forecasting {horizon} steps: "
            f"{n_rows} training rows after feature engineering, need > {horizon}"
        )
    future = _future_exog(X_exog, X_future, horizon)
    exog = _exog_matrix(X_exog) if X_exog is not None else None
    offset = len(y_train) - n_rows  # time index of the first feature row
    params = _estimator_kwargs(estimator_class, random_state, use_gpu, model_params)
    lags_next = next_step_features(y_train, n_lags, n_rolling)

    predictions = np.empty(horizon)
    for h in range(horizon):
        X_h, x_next = X_lags[: n_rows - h], lags_next
        if exog is not None and future is not None:
            X_h = np.hstack([X_h, exog[offset + h: offset + n_rows]])
            x_next = np.hstack([lags_next, future[h: h + 1]])
        predictions[h] = _fit_predict(estimator_class(**params), X_h, y_feat[h:], x_next)[0]
    return predictions

def multi_output_forecast(
    estimator_class,
    y_train: np.ndarray,
    horizon: int,
    n_lags: int = 10,
    n_rolling: Tuple[int, ...] = (3, 7),
    X_exog: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    random_state: int = 42,
    use_gpu: bool = False,
    model_params: Optional[dict] = None,
    X_future: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Multi-output forecasting: predict all horizon steps at once.

    Uses sklearn's MultiOutputRegressor to learn ``y[t], ..., y[t + horizon - 1]``
    from the lag features available at time ``t`` and, with exogenous
    variables, all their values from ``t`` to ``t + horizon - 1``; then
    predicts every step from the lags after ``y_train`` and ``X_future``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    estimator_class : type
        Sklearn-compatible regressor class.
    y_train : np.ndarray
        Training time series.
    horizon : int
        Number of future steps.
    n_lags : int
        Number of lag features.
    n_rolling : tuple of int
        Rolling window sizes.
    X_exog : np.ndarray or None
        Exogenous features for the training period.
    random_state : int
        Random seed.
    use_gpu : bool
        Whether to use GPU.
    model_params : dict or None
        Extra model constructor params.
    X_future : np.ndarray or None
        Exogenous features for the forecast period, one row per step
        (required with ``X_exog``).

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Array of length ``horizon``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``y_train`` is too short for the requested horizon.
    """
    X_lags, y_feat = create_lag_features(y_train, n_lags, n_rolling)
    n_samples = len(y_feat) - horizon + 1
    if n_samples < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Not enough history for multi-output forecasting {horizon} steps: "
            f"{len(y_feat)} training rows after feature engineering"
        )
    future = _future_exog(X_exog, X_future, horizon)
    Y_multi = np.column_stack([y_feat[h:n_samples + h] for h in range(horizon)])
    X_rows, x_next = X_lags[:n_samples], next_step_features(y_train, n_lags, n_rolling)
    if X_exog is not None and future is not None:
        # Every step's exogenous values: rows t .. t + horizon - 1.
        exog = _exog_matrix(X_exog)
        offset = len(y_train) - len(y_feat)
        X_rows = np.hstack([X_rows] + [exog[offset + h: offset + h + n_samples] for h in range(horizon)])
        x_next = np.hstack([x_next, future.reshape(1, -1)])
    params = _estimator_kwargs(estimator_class, random_state, use_gpu, model_params)
    multi_model = MultiOutputRegressor(estimator_class(**params))
    return np.asarray(_fit_predict(multi_model, X_rows, Y_multi, x_next)[0])

    scores_df: pd.DataFrame,
    metric: str = "RMSE",
    top_k: int = 10,
    figsize: Tuple[int, int] = (10, 6),
    ax: Optional[Any] = None,

def plot_residuals(
    y_true: np.ndarray,
    y_pred: np.ndarray,
    model_name: Optional[str] = None,
    seasonal_period: int = 1,
    figsize: Tuple[int, int] = (12, 10),
) -> Any:
    """Four-panel residual diagnostic plot.

    Panels:
        1. Residuals over time (scatter with zero line)
        2. Histogram of residuals
        3. QQ plot against normal distribution
        4. ACF of residuals with confidence bands

    Parameters
    ----------
    y_true : np.ndarray
        Actual values.
    y_pred : np.ndarray
        Predicted values.
    model_name : str or None
        Model name for the title.
    seasonal_period : int
        Seasonal period for ACF display.
    figsize : tuple
        Figure size.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
    """
    _check_matplotlib()

    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)
    y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float)
    residuals = y_true - y_pred

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=figsize)
    title = f"Residual Diagnostics — {model_name}" if model_name else "Residual Diagnostics"
    fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=14)

    # Panel 1: Residuals over time
    ax1 = axes[0, 0]
    ax1.scatter(range(len(residuals)), residuals, s=20, alpha=0.7, color="steelblue")
    ax1.axhline(y=0, color="red", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
    ax1.set_xlabel("Index")
    ax1.set_ylabel("Residual")
    ax1.set_title("Residuals Over Time")

    # Panel 2: Histogram
    ax2 = axes[0, 1]
    ax2.hist(residuals, bins="auto", density=True, alpha=0.7, color="steelblue", edgecolor="white")
    # Overlay normal curve
    mu, sigma = np.mean(residuals), np.std(residuals)
    if sigma > 0:
        x_norm = np.linspace(mu - 4 * sigma, mu + 4 * sigma, 100)
        y_norm = (1 / (sigma * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x_norm - mu) / sigma) ** 2)
        ax2.plot(x_norm, y_norm, color="red", linewidth=1.5, label="Normal")
        ax2.legend(fontsize=8)
    ax2.set_xlabel("Residual")
    ax2.set_ylabel("Density")
    ax2.set_title("Residual Distribution")

    # Panel 3: QQ Plot
    ax3 = axes[1, 0]
    sorted_residuals = np.sort(residuals)
    n = len(sorted_residuals)
    theoretical_quantiles = np.array([
        _norm_ppf((i - 0.5) / n) for i in range(1, n + 1)
    ])
    ax3.scatter(theoretical_quantiles, sorted_residuals, s=20, alpha=0.7, color="steelblue")
    # Reference line
    q1_idx, q3_idx = max(0, n // 4 - 1), min(n - 1, 3 * n // 4 - 1)
    if q3_idx > q1_idx:
        tq1, tq3 = theoretical_quantiles[q1_idx], theoretical_quantiles[q3_idx]
        sq1, sq3 = sorted_residuals[q1_idx], sorted_residuals[q3_idx]
        slope = (sq3 - sq1) / (tq3 - tq1) if tq3 != tq1 else 1
        intercept = sq1 - slope * tq1
        line_x = np.array([theoretical_quantiles[0], theoretical_quantiles[-1]])
        ax3.plot(line_x, slope * line_x + intercept, color="red", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
    ax3.set_xlabel("Theoretical Quantiles")
    ax3.set_ylabel("Sample Quantiles")
    ax3.set_title("Q-Q Plot")

    # Panel 4: ACF
    ax4 = axes[1, 1]
    max_lag = min(len(residuals) - 1, max(20, 2 * seasonal_period))
    acf_values = _compute_acf(residuals, max_lag)
    conf_bound = 1.96 / np.sqrt(len(residuals))
    ax4.bar(range(len(acf_values)), acf_values, width=0.3, color="steelblue")
    ax4.axhline(y=conf_bound, color="red", linestyle="--", linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.7)
    ax4.axhline(y=-conf_bound, color="red", linestyle="--", linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.7)
    ax4.axhline(y=0, color="black", linewidth=0.5)
    ax4.set_xlabel("Lag")
    ax4.set_ylabel("ACF")
    ax4.set_title("Autocorrelation of Residuals")

    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.96))
    return fig

def plot_error_distribution(
    y_true: np.ndarray,
    predictions: Dict[str, np.ndarray],
    figsize: Tuple[int, int] = (10, 6),
    ax: Optional[Any] = None,
) -> Any:
    """Box plot of absolute errors across models.

    Parameters
    ----------
    y_true : np.ndarray
        Actual values.
    predictions : dict
        ``{model_name: y_pred}`` dict.
    figsize : tuple
        Figure size.
    ax : matplotlib Axes or None
        Axes to plot on.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
    """
    _check_matplotlib()

    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)
    if not predictions:
        raise ValueError("No predictions provided.")

    if ax is None:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    else:
        fig = ax.get_figure()

    error_data = []
    labels = []
    for name, y_pred in predictions.items():
        y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float)
        abs_errors = np.abs(y_true[: len(y_pred)] - y_pred)
        error_data.append(abs_errors)
        labels.append(name)

    bp = ax.boxplot(error_data, patch_artist=True)
    ax.set_xticks(range(1, len(labels) + 1), labels)  # tick_labels= needs matplotlib >= 3.9
    colors = plt.cm.Set2(np.linspace(0, 1, len(error_data)))
    for patch, color in zip(bp["boxes"], colors):
        patch.set_facecolor(color)

    ax.set_ylabel("Absolute Error")
    ax.set_title("Error Distribution by Model")
    if len(labels) > 5:
        ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
    fig.tight_layout()
    return fig

def plot_metrics_heatmap(
    scores_df: pd.DataFrame,
    metrics: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    figsize: Tuple[int, int] = (10, 8),
    ax: Optional[Any] = None,
) -> Any:
    """Heatmap of normalized metrics across models.

    Metrics are min-max normalized to [0, 1] for visual comparison.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores_df : pd.DataFrame
        Scores table from ``LazyForecaster.fit()``.
    metrics : list of str or None
        Metric columns to include. Defaults to MAE, RMSE, MAPE, SMAPE, MASE.
    figsize : tuple
        Figure size.
    ax : matplotlib Axes or None
        Axes to plot on.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
    """
    _check_matplotlib()

    if metrics is None:
        metrics = [m for m in ["MAE", "RMSE", "MAPE", "SMAPE", "MASE"] if m in scores_df.columns]
    if not metrics:
        raise ValueError("No valid metrics found in scores DataFrame.")

    data = scores_df[metrics].dropna()
    if data.empty:
        raise ValueError("No data to plot after dropping NaN values.")

    # Min-max normalize each column
    normalized = data.copy()
    for col in metrics:
        col_min, col_max = data[col].min(), data[col].max()
        if col_max > col_min:
            normalized[col] = (data[col] - col_min) / (col_max - col_min)
        else:
            normalized[col] = 0.0

    if ax is None:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    else:
        fig = ax.get_figure()

    im = ax.imshow(normalized.values, cmap="RdYlGn_r", aspect="auto")
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(metrics)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(metrics, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(normalized)))
    ax.set_yticklabels(normalized.index, fontsize=9)

    # Annotate with original values
    for i in range(len(normalized)):
        for j in range(len(metrics)):
            val = data.iloc[i, j]
            text_color = "white" if normalized.iloc[i, j] > 0.6 else "black"
            ax.text(j, i, f"{val:.2f}", ha="center", va="center",
                    fontsize=8, color=text_color)

    ax.set_title("Metrics Heatmap (normalized)")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8, label="Normalized (lower=better)")
    fig.tight_layout()
    return fig

def residual_diagnostics(
    y_true: np.ndarray,
    y_pred: np.ndarray,
    y_train: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    seasonal_period: int = 1,
    max_lags: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Compute comprehensive residual diagnostics.

    Parameters
    ----------
    y_true : array-like
        Actual values.
    y_pred : array-like
        Predicted values.
    y_train : array-like or None
        Training data (unused currently, reserved for future MASE-based tests).
    seasonal_period : int
        Seasonal period for selecting ACF lag count.
    max_lags : int or None
        Maximum number of ACF lags. Defaults to ``min(len(residuals)-1, max(10, 2*seasonal_period))``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Keys:
        - ``residuals``: np.ndarray — raw residuals (y_true - y_pred)
        - ``mean``: float — mean of residuals (should be near 0)
        - ``std``: float — standard deviation of residuals
        - ``ljung_box_stat``: float or None — Ljung-Box Q statistic
        - ``ljung_box_pvalue``: float or None — p-value (>0.05 = white noise)
        - ``jarque_bera_stat``: float or None — Jarque-Bera statistic
        - ``jarque_bera_pvalue``: float or None — p-value (>0.05 = normal)
        - ``acf_values``: np.ndarray — autocorrelation values
        - ``is_white_noise``: bool — True if Ljung-Box p > 0.05
        - ``is_normal``: bool — True if Jarque-Bera p > 0.05
    """
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)
    y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float)
    residuals = y_true - y_pred
    n = len(residuals)

    if max_lags is None:
        max_lags = min(n - 1, max(10, 2 * seasonal_period))
    max_lags = max(1, min(max_lags, n - 1))

    result: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "residuals": residuals,
        "mean": float(np.mean(residuals)),
        "std": float(np.std(residuals, ddof=1)) if n > 1 else 0.0,
    }
    result["acf_values"] = _compute_acf(residuals, max_lags)
    result.update(_ljung_box(residuals, max_lags))
    result.update(_jarque_bera(residuals))
    return result

    y_true: np.ndarray,
    predictions: Dict[str, np.ndarray],
    y_train: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,

def auto_convert_dataframe(
    data: Any, name: str = "data"
) -> Union[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series, np.ndarray]:
    """Auto-convert PySpark or Dask DataFrames to pandas.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : any
        Input data — may be pandas, PySpark, Dask, or numpy.
    name : str
        Label for log messages.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame, pandas.Series, or numpy.ndarray
        Converted data.
    """
    cls_name = type(data).__module__ + "." + type(data).__name__

    # PySpark DataFrame
    if "pyspark.sql" in cls_name and hasattr(data, "toPandas"):
        logger.warning(
            "Auto-converting PySpark DataFrame (%s) to pandas via .toPandas(). "
            "This collects all data to the driver node.",
            name,
        )
        return data.toPandas()

    # Dask DataFrame / Series
    if "dask.dataframe" in cls_name and hasattr(data, "compute"):
        logger.warning(
            "Auto-converting Dask DataFrame (%s) to pandas via .compute(). "
            "This materializes the full dataset in memory.",
            name,
        )
        return data.compute()

    # Dask Array
    if "dask.array" in cls_name and hasattr(data, "compute"):
        logger.warning(
            "Auto-converting Dask Array (%s) to numpy via .compute().",
            name,
        )
        return data.compute()

    return data

def register_dask_backend() -> bool:
    """Register Dask as a joblib parallel backend if available.

    Call this before cross-validation to distribute folds across
    Dask workers. Returns True if registration succeeded.

    Usage
    -----
    >>> from lazypredict.distributed import register_dask_backend
    >>> if register_dask_backend():
    ...     # Now cross_validate will use Dask workers
    ...     pass
    """
    global _dask_backend_registered
    if _dask_backend_registered:
        return True

    try:
        from dask.distributed import Client

        # Register dask as a parallel backend
        try:
            from joblib import parallel_config  # noqa: F401
            # joblib >= 1.3 uses parallel_config
            _dask_backend_registered = True
        except ImportError:
            pass

        # Check if a client is already running
        try:
            client = Client.current()
            logger.info(
                "Dask client found at %s — using Dask for parallel CV.",
                client.dashboard_link or "local",
            )
        except ValueError:
            # No client running, create a local one
            client = Client(processes=False, silence_logs=logging.WARNING)
            logger.info(
                "Created local Dask client for parallel CV."
            )
        _dask_backend_registered = True
        return True

    except ImportError:
        logger.info(
            "dask.distributed not available — using default joblib backend."
        )
        return False

def get_dask_joblib_context():
    """Return a joblib parallel_config context manager for Dask, or None.

    Usage
    -----
    >>> ctx = get_dask_joblib_context()
    >>> if ctx:
    ...     with ctx:
    ...         cross_validate(...)
    """
    if not _dask_backend_registered:
        if not register_dask_backend():
            return None

    try:
        from joblib import parallel_config
        return parallel_config(backend="dask")
    except (ImportError, Exception):
        return None

        try:
            model = cls(
                labelCol=self.label_col,
                featuresCol=self.features_col,
            )
            pipe = SparkPipeline(stages=[assembler, model])
            fitted = pipe.fit(train_df)
            predictions = fitted.transform(test_df)

            )
            precision = evaluator.evaluate(
                predictions, {evaluator.metricName: "weightedPrecision"}
            )
            recall = evaluator.evaluate(
                predictions, {evaluator.metricName: "weightedRecall"}
            )

            self.models[name] = fitted
            elapsed = time.time() - start
            results.append({
                "Model": name,
                "Accuracy": accuracy,
                "F1 Score": f1,
                "Precision": precision,
                "Recall": recall,
                "Time Taken": elapsed,
            })

            if self.verbose > 0:

        except Exception as exc:
